sharedMapEvidence: None. This is a deliberate split from epever-tracer-a, not an oversight. G3 is a new generation - it adds BMS-Link lithium-BMS bridging, a Primary/Secondary port mode, and an enable/disable switch on the RS-485 port, none of which exist on the XTRA-N or Tracer AN the community implementations were written against. gotchas: The RS-485 port can be switched off from the LCD (PV parameters -> CON -> DIS). Disabled, it supplies neither the 5 V nor any communication, and the manual notes self-consumption drops - so a silent bus may be a setting, not a fault.

Primary/Secondary port mode: 'The Primary mode is used for BMS communication; the Secondary mode is used for RS485 communication.' A G3 left in Primary (nn) mode will not answer a host poll. It must show S.

G3 units pair with a BMS-Link module and carry a per-manufacturer 'BMS protocol number' for translating third-party lithium BMS protocols. That is a second protocol surface on the same controller, entirely undocumented publicly.

The Canadian retail name 'iTracer AN G3 60A' does not match EPEver's own catalogue name for the same rating ('IT-NC G3 Series 50~100A'). Do not assume the retail name maps to the vendor series - confirm on the label.

EPEver's current documents page (epever.com/support/documents/, checked 2026-07-31) publishes no controller Modbus protocol PDF at all. The only protocol documents it offers are BMS-Link ones. The controller protocol documents that exist are all older and hosted by third parties.
